docs/glossary.md:19:| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol — DataQ exposes 46 curated tools at `/mcp` for AI assistants (23 read-only, 18 that change state, 5 live-probe tools gated like writes). |
docs/architecture.md:564:- **The `/mcp` endpoint exposes the same service layer to AI clients.** The 8 FastMCP tools are thin wrappers reusing the same services + per-suite authz + sample redaction as the REST API — no logic duplication. It mounts under **any** of the three sign-in modes (SSO, email OTP, dev-bypass) and stays unmounted, **fail-closed**, only when none is configured. Under SSO it validates the same OIDC bearer (Azure AD or Cognito — a `JWTVerifier` on the same tenant/audience/scope) or a PAT; **under email OTP a PAT is the only accepted credential** — a raw JWT and a session cookie are both rejected there, since there is no IdP-issued bearer to validate and a session is a browser-only credential ([#1151](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1151)). See [ADR 0008](adr/0008-mcp-server.md) / [ADR 0032](adr/0032-email-otp-signin.md).

**Chosen scope is 4a:** a vetted, server-served superset of GX's ~50 built-ins — the existing catalog pattern scaled up. **Explicitly not 4b** (an open marketplace of arbitrary/community \`Expectation\` classes — a code-execution / supply-chain risk; such classes would have to be image-installed, pinned and reviewed, never loaded dynamically).

**The useful irony is the real deliverable:** doing 4a safely means adding the **server-side allowlist v1 deliberately lacks** — today \`gx_runner\` title-cases *any* \`expectation_type\` string into a GX class and \`checks.config\` is free-form JSONB. Flip that convenience into a vetted catalog the backend validates submitted \`expectation_type\`s against. This also hardens LLM-generated output (SQL-gen / suggestions issues) and MCP \`create_check\`/\`update_check\`/\`import_suite\` inputs.

Depends on / extends #1509 (the built-ins batch)." | tail -1
gh issue create --title "feat: LLMProvider seam — admin-configured outbound LLM, BYO credential, default-off" --label enhancement --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --body "From [docs/post-v1-dq-intelligence-notes.md](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/post-v1-dq-intelligence-notes.md) §LLM integration model (roadmap Theme 2; also the enabler for Theme 2's agentic root-cause narrative — one seam, multiple features).

v1 has no outbound-LLM capability (the MCP server is the opposite direction). The seam mirrors \`ConnectionAdapter\` / \`SecretStore\` / \`OrchestrationProvider\`:

- **Workspace-admin-configured, one provider** (provider + endpoint + model + credential), credential in the \`SecretStore\`. Per-user keys deferred as an optional override.
- **Default OFF + graceful degradation** — the app fully works with no LLM configured; LLM features are additive.
- **Pluggable impls (ADR 0010/0013, no hardcoded vendor):** Anthropic API (default), Azure AI Foundry/OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the 'local LLM' answer — Ollama/vLLM/TGI; nothing baked into the image per ADR 0025). Largely \`{base_url, api_key, model, auth_adapter}\` + a structured-output capability flag with prompt-JSON fallback.
- **Cost ownership = the customer's (BYOL).** Never proxy through a key we own (contra ADR 0013).
- **PII discipline is a hard requirement:** schema + aggregate profiler stats only, never raw sample rows / PII-column values (reuse the redaction seam). The local-endpoint impl exists for customers who can't send even schema out. This is also the compliance-posture 'LLM transfer minimization' row (G4 lists the seam as an enumerated-while-disabled transfer).
- **Runs on the Celery worker**, not the request path. Record the decision as an ADR when built.

A real platform DQ feature is a first-class **channel** entity: define a Teams/Slack/email destination once, reference it from many suites (and severities); rotating a webhook then touches one place instead of N suites.

Notes:

input.new_string:
| **Check** | One data-quality rule — a Great Expectations *expectation*, or a monitor kind (below). |
| **Expectation** | A Great Expectations assertion about data (e.g. "column not null"). |
| **Monitor** | A non-expectation check kind: *freshness* (staleness), *volume* (row-count range), *schema_drift* (column add/drop/retype vs a baseline), *anomaly* (rolling z-score over metric history), or *comparison* (cross-dataset reconciliation). |
| **Dimension** | A check's DQ-dimension classification (ADR 0038): accuracy / completeness / consistency / integrity / timeliness / uniqueness / validity. NULL = unclassified, rendered as a coverage gap. |

| **Trigger binding** | A mapping `(provider, pipeline/DAG, env) → suite` that runs a suite when a pipeline succeeds. |
| **Asset** | The table/path a suite targets, as a first-class entity — OpenLineage `(namespace, name)` identity (ADR 0034); workspace-visible, with suite-derived detail behind grants (ADR 0037). |
| **Lineage edge** | A cached upstream→downstream asset dependency pulled from systems that already know it (dbt manifest, warehouse APIs) — never authored in DataQ. |
| **Incident** | The stateful, deduped object failing results roll up into: `open → acknowledged → resolved`, ≤1 active per (asset, check), evidence card attached (ADR 0034). |

1	# DataQ v1.1.0 — retrospective
2	
3	> Internal document (excluded from the published site). Written 2026-08-15 at the
4	> `v1.1.0` tag, closing the six-week post-v1 cycle (2026-07-04 → 2026-08-15).
5	> Companion to [progress.md](progress.md) (the live per-PR tracker, §Cycle plan)
6	> and [retro-v1.md](retro-v1.md) (the v1 retro this one builds on). The W7
7	> stretch milestone (backlog burn-down, due 2026-08-22) stays open past the tag
8	> — see "What rolls" below.
9	
10	## What shipped
11	
12	The leap from "GX runner" to DQ platform that the v1 retro forecast: all five
13	reserved monitor kinds are now real (`comparison` W3 · `schema_drift` W4 ·
14	`anomaly` W5, joining freshness/volume), classified on the ADR 0038 dimension
15	axis and rolled into asset scorecards; the G-d assets/lineage/incidents track
16	end-to-end (asset entity on OpenLineage naming, OL emission + dbt manifests +
17	warehouse `GET_LINEAGE` pull, incidents with evidence cards, the nav inversion);
18	scale-aware execution (G-b) — sampling + partition batching + an OOM guardrail
19	that refuses instead of SIGKILLing, with sampled-ness recorded per result and
20	surfaced through UI, report, and exports; Iceberg as a fifth datasource (native
21	`pyiceberg`, ADR 0030) and S3-compatible stores (MinIO/R2/…, #1063); the email
22	OTP authenticator (ADR 0032, Mailpit-backed local default) and rate limiting
23	(ADR 0035); the OpenBao secret-store seam (ADR 0039) that ended
24	plaintext-Redis-by-default and Azure-only production secrets; warehouse
25	inventory sync (ADR 0040); the history/audit decision (ADR 0041); honest
26	incremental run progress; and a hardening tail measured in the hundreds
27	(dependency/CodeQL/supply-chain triages, perf batches, flake kills).
28	
29	**By the numbers:** 498 commits · ~434 issues/PRs closed across the six weekly
30	milestones + 253 in the rolling Backlog milestone · **14 new ADRs** (0028–0041)
31	· backend tests 1,289 → **4,180** (97.25%, gate ≥80%) · frontend 337 → **1,012**
32	· issue/PR numbers #571 → #1335 consumed in six weeks.
33	
34	## What worked (keep doing)
35	
36	- **The #953 rule — "for anything crossing a driver boundary, only a live run is
37	  evidence" — earned its name over and over.** This cycle alone: UC freshness
38	  had *never* worked (driver returns MAX-of-TIMESTAMP as `str`); the profiler's
39	  obvious `UNION ALL` batching compiled cleanly and was refused by a live
40	  engine; `TABLESAMPLE (6e-05 PERCENT)` — Python float repr — was a live parse
41	  error on exactly the huge-table case the feature targets; two stacked crashes
42	  hid in one Snowflake SQL literal. Every one was invisible to a green,
43	  well-covered suite, and every one fell out of a live pre-merge run. W6 made
44	  live verification a **merge gate** for driver-boundary PRs, not a post-merge
45	  chore — keep it there.
46	- **Mandated multi-angle review before merge, with mutation-checked fixes.**
47	  The W6 close batch alone surfaced ~40 real findings pre-merge, including two
48	  **pre-existing production bugs** found by reviewing adjacent code (the
49	  profiler `freq` alias capture; the API silently dropping a suite's `sampling`
50	  block — the feature under review was unreachable and its own tests passed).
51	  The review fan-outs also repeatedly caught the reviewer-proof failure mode:
52	  regression tests that pass against the unfixed code (three rewritten in W6
53	  after mutation checks).
54	- **Fixed-or-filed, no pre-existing excuse.** Every review finding in the cycle
55	  ended as an in-PR fix or a numbered issue; "verified-benign" got recorded with
56	  evidence. The follow-up graph (#1318–#1320, #1326–#1331, #1334…) is the
57	  planning input for the next cycle, for free.
58	- **Subscription-driven sequencing.** Front-loading everything that needed the
59	  expiring Snowflake/Azure subscriptions (W1–W3), then running cloud-independent
60	  (W4–W6), meant zero deadline-forced compromises when the wind-down windows
61	  arrived.
62	- **Seams keep absorbing change.** ADR 0039 dropped a fourth SecretStore behind
63	  the Week-2 seam untouched; the monitor-kind discriminator took three new kinds
64	  without a schema rewrite; ADR 0036's connection-anchored engines and ADR
65	  0041's audit log both slot behind existing seams.
66	
67	## What hurt (do differently)
68	
69	- **The orchestration that made the cycle fast nearly ended it.** Parallel
70	  implementation agents + 4–8-finder review fan-outs delivered the W5 and W6
71	  batches in single sessions — and blew through the monthly spend limit **four
72	  times** in the close-out session, each kill leaving an agent mid-edit and
73	  costing a recovery pass. Standing directive recorded (memory +
74	  this document): work **inline and sequentially**, smallest-fan-out reviews,
75	  one at a time, until the budget posture changes. Scale of orchestration is now
76	  a resource decision, not a default.
77	- **A CONFLICTING PR gets zero CI, silently.** When `main` moved under PR #1325,
78	  GitHub stopped building the test-merge commit — so no `pull_request` events,
79	  no Actions runs, presenting as "CI stopped scheduling" and costing a day of
80	  misdiagnosis (delivery incident? Actions outage?). The fix is trivial (merge
81	  main into the branch); the *diagnosis* is the lesson: `mergeable:
82	  CONFLICTING` is the first thing to check when runs vanish.
83	- **Tracker rows rot when closes happen elsewhere.** The W6 table sat at 0/14
84	  while 8 of its rows had been closed by earlier batches under other headings —
85	  the same point-in-time-counts lesson as v1, now on checkbox state. The
86	  merge-hook nudge helps only if the row exists where the close happens; a
87	  weekly reconcile against `gh issue list` (not memory) is the durable habit.
88	- **Per-phase commits are a systemic contract change, not a local one.** #1332's
89	  review found the cycle's sharpest architecture lesson: making result rows
90	  visible mid-run silently broke three consumers that relied on
91	  "only terminal succeeded runs have rows" (rollups, alert dedup, baseline
92	  durability). The fix — a shared `AGGREGATABLE_RUN_STATUSES` read-side filter —
93	  is the pattern: when a write-side invariant weakens, make the read side own
94	  the rule, in one place.
95	
96	## Decisions of record (2026-08-15)
97	
98	- **Sequential, no-agents working mode** until the credit posture changes
99	  (user directive; supersedes the batch-3-4 guidance).
100	- **Iceberg scan cap deferred to its own measurement** (#1328): inheriting
101	  `RUN_MAX_SCAN_ROWS` would refuse a rung Iceberg is measured to survive.
102	- **Per-check GX increments declined by design** (#318/#1332): splitting the
103	  atomic batch would re-read the dataset per check; the honest fallback
104	  (heartbeat + server elapsed) is the deliverable.
105	- **Check ordering ordinal deferred** (#1334): `CHECK_ORDER` is honest where
106	  authoring times differ; same-transaction imports tie and need a real ordinal.
107	
108	## Final verification before the tag
109	
110	- All six W6 issues closed with CI green on every merge; the two
111	  driver-boundary PRs (#1323, #1325) live-verified **pre-merge** against real
112	  Snowflake + Unity Catalog (equivalence, type fidelity, TABLESAMPLE/
113	  REPEATABLE semantics, no 25-way-join planner cliff).
114	- Zero open PRs at the tag; the W6 milestone holds only the cycle epic (#597),
115	  closed with it.
116	- Backend 4,180 tests / 97.25% and frontend 1,012 tests green on `main`;
117	  both migrations in the release (`fbf4fe92e295`, `4d23b47ee564`) are additive
118	  and tested up/down/up.
119	
120	## What rolls (explicitly, never silently)
121	
122	The **W7 stretch milestone** (due 2026-08-22) stays open past this tag with its
123	11 issues: the compliance track G1–G5 (#431–#435), MCP tier-1 expansion (#529),
124	and the remaining backlog burn-down candidates. Whatever remains at its close
125	rolls to the next cycle's planning **by name**, per the standing rule. The next
126	cycle's inputs are this document, the open follow-up graph above, and
127	[context/post-v1-roadmap.md](../context/post-v1-roadmap.md).

1	# Changelog
2	
3	Notable, user-facing changes. Dates are the release/merge date. This is a curated summary —
4	the per-PR history lives in the repo's commit log and pull requests.
5	
6	## Unreleased — v1.1 (in progress)
7	
8	Portability, auto-monitors, and polish on top of v1:
9	
10	- ⚠️ **Workspace roles — Admin / Member / Viewer (ADR 0033)** — authorization is now two
11	  axes. Your **workspace role** says what kind of user you are; the existing per-suite
12	  `view / edit / admin / owner` grants say what you can touch. Neither replaces the other:
13	  a Member with no share on a suite still cannot see it.
14	
15	  | Capability | Admin | Member | Viewer |
16	  |---|---|---|---|
17	  | See/use suites shared to them | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (view only) |
18	  | Create/import suites (become owner) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
19	  | Receive `edit` shares | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ — capped at `view` |
20	  | Connections: create / edit / delete / re-auth | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
21	  | Connections: list & reference in suites | ✅ | ✅ | list only |
22	  | Connections: test | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
23	  | `/admin`, implicit suite-admin, workspace-wide visibility | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
24	
25	  **BREAKING — Members lose connection-write.** Previously *any* authenticated user could
26	  delete or re-credential the connection every suite in the workspace ran on. If people who
27	  are not workspace admins manage connections in your deployment, **promote them to Admin
28	  before upgrading**, or those operations will start returning 403.
29	
30	  Everything else upgrades with **no config change**: existing users become Members (which
31	  is exactly what they could already do), and `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` keeps resolving to
32	  Admin — it is now a **bootstrap seed and lockout break-glass** rather than the admin
33	  mechanism, and it only ever grants, never demotes. New: `AUTH_OTP_DEFAULT_ROLE` /
34	  `AUTH_OIDC_DEFAULT_ROLE` set the tier new signups land on (`member` by default; set
35	  `viewer` when your signup allowlist is a whole domain).
36	
37	  Roles resolve **per request**, so a change takes effect on the target's next request —
38	  including requests made with their existing API tokens, which authenticate as their user.
39	  There is no token to revoke.
40	
41	- **Security hardening across both reference deployments** —
42	  ([#1386](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1386),
43	  [#1387](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1387),
44	  [#1388](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1388)):
45	  - **Who may hold an account is now an explicit decision.** DataQ provisions a user on first
46	    successful OIDC sign-in, so the identity provider's registration policy was in effect the
47	    product's access policy. The AWS reference pool is now admin-create-only, and a new
48	    app-side allowlist (`OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS` / `OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`) is enforced on every
49	    request — on REST **and** MCP — so it revokes as well as admits.
50	  - **Browser security headers on every response** — CSP, HSTS, `X-Frame-Options`,
51	    `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`. The CSP matters here because the UI
52	    renders warehouse-supplied content (failing-row samples, error text).
53	  - **Edge protection on AWS** — a CloudFront WAF per-IP rate ceiling in front of the in-app
54	    limiter (which fails open by design), plus edge caching of the fingerprinted bundle so
55	    the distribution actually absorbs load instead of passing everything through.
56	
57	- **AWS as a second deployment target** — a live-verified OpenTofu reference stack
58	  ([`deploy/terraform/aws/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/aws)):
59	  ECS Fargate (api / worker / frontend) + RDS + ElastiCache + **Amazon Cognito** (via the
60	  same generic OIDC contract) + **AWS Secrets Manager** (`SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`,
61	  a fourth secret backend) behind **CloudFront** with an nginx-enforced origin secret;
62	  **SES email alerts**, **X-Ray tracing** through an ADOT sidecar on the app's
63	  vendor-neutral OTLP export, and a dedicated **Deploy (AWS)** GitHub Actions workflow.
64	  Azure remains the primary reference deployment.
65	- **dbt as a third orchestration provider** — observe dbt builds and trigger suites on
66	  success, via a post-build HMAC callback + a `run_results.json` artifact poll (ADR 0029).
67	- **Apache Iceberg as a fifth datasource** — native `pyiceberg` read (v2 baseline; ADR
68	  0030, #716/#722), with natively-computed freshness/volume monitors, a column profiler +
69	  column listing, and dry-run preview (#721).
70	- **Freshness & volume monitors** — the first auto-monitor kinds (is the data stale? did the
71	  load land whole?) on SQL datasources plus Iceberg.
72	- **Vendor-neutral observability** — OpenTelemetry logs + traces, exportable to Application
73	  Insights and/or a generic OTLP endpoint.
74	- **Personal access tokens (PATs)** — `dq_live_` tokens for headless / AI-client use, on REST
75	  and MCP (ADR 0026).
76	- **Workspace-admin visibility** extended to the MCP tools + schedules; **dry-run preview**
77	  extended to every datasource.
78	- **Every MCP tool now states what it cannot see.** A REST caller wrote their own
79	  query and a UI user reads the screen; an AI client has neither, so a tool that
80	  returns literally-true values while omitting its blind spot produces a
81	  confident wrong answer. All 46 were audited against six criteria — population,
82	  time window, truncation, freshness, null/zero semantics, and what the tool
83	  structurally cannot see — and the limits are returned as **fields** wherever
84	  possible rather than prose: `truncated` / `oldest_in_page` (the list tools take
85	  no time filter), `results_final` (a mid-run partial is not a verdict),
86	  `redaction` / `redacted_columns` (a masked sample is not an absent one),
87	  `sampled` / `sample_row_limit` (flat-file and Iceberg profiles read at most
88	  100k rows), `runnable`, `is_recurrence`, `window_hours`. Six docstrings were
89	  corrected outright, having claimed things the code does not do — see
90	  [AI assistants (MCP setup)](mcp-setup.md) under *Reading the results honestly*.
91	- **MCP server expanded to 46 tools** — the Tier 1 read-only batch (checks, runs,
92	  connections, schedules, trigger bindings, notification config, suite performance,
93	  suite export) alongside the original 8, plus the Tier 2 batch (update/delete/snooze
94	  check, dry-run preview, cancel run, schedule + trigger-binding CRUD, suggest a PII
95	  policy, test a connection, import a suite), plus the Tier 3A coherence batch
96	  (set a suite's run target, read/set its column policy, update a schedule,
97	  update/delete a trigger binding, read and restore a check's version history), plus the
98	  Tier 3B batch over **assets and incidents** (browse the tables DataQ monitors with
99	  their health and lineage; see what is broken right now and the evidence behind it,
100	  acknowledge and resolve it, list a target's columns before authoring, and diagnose
101	  orchestration triggers that are silently never firing) — each reusing the same
102	  authorization its REST counterpart applies (ADR 0008 amendments,
103	  #529 / #1424). The 46 split three ways: 23
104	  read-only; 18 that change state, gated on `edit` access to the suite they act on; and
105	  5 that persist nothing but open a live datasource connection with stored credentials
106	  (`profile_column`, `list_columns`, `dryrun_check`, `suggest_column_policy`,
107	  `test_connection`) — gated
108	  like writes, not reads, and requiring the **member** workspace role where there is no
109	  suite to gate on. No MCP tool is Admin-only: every Admin-only capability in ADR 0033's
110	  matrix is a connection mutation, and none are exposed here. `list_connections` returns
111	  metadata + health only, never config or secrets; `get_notification_config` reports
112	  channel presence, never webhook URLs; `test_connection` reports only pass/fail, never
113	  a credential; connection create/update/reauth remain excluded — a credential must
114	  never transit an LLM.
115	- **Run failure reasons** — a run that fails to execute now shows a redaction-safe reason.
116	- **Secret lifecycle** — connection delete cleans up its stored secret.
117	- **Assets as the primary lens** — a data asset (table/file) is now a first-class entity
118	  with its own page: health rolled up across every suite that targets it, open incidents,
119	  and lineage. The dashboard and sidebar lead with assets; suites and runs link back to
120	  the asset they touch (ADR 0034).
121	- **Lineage graph** — an asset's provenance and blast radius render as one left-to-right
122	  graph, one column per hop, with clickable nodes.
123	- **Asset browse by source** — drill down datasource → database → schema → table, with a
124	  flat searchable table as the second lens.
125	- **Two health axes on an asset** — "could DataQ reach the datasource?" is shown separately
126	  from "is the data good?", so an unreachable datasource no longer masquerades as a data
127	  failure, and a run that evaluated nothing no longer reads as a green pass.
128	- **Datasources read as names** — the UI shows `Snowflake · ACCT` / `ADLS · account/container`
129	  / `iceberg_catalog` instead of the raw connection string (an Iceberg namespace is a full
130	  DSN). The raw identifier stays available on hover and via copy.
131	- **Mobile** — the sidebar becomes an overlay drawer on a narrow viewport, and the share /
132	  edit panels reflow so their controls stay on screen (previously the "Add" button in the
133	  share drawer was painted off the right edge, making a suite unshareable from a phone).
134	- **A broken orchestration poll now tells you** — an expired credential silently stopped
135	  pipeline-run ingest, suite triggering, and lineage refresh for six days in our own
136	  production. A failing poll is now a fact about the connection: the connections list badges
137	  it with a failure count, the lineage panel warns instead of showing a confident empty
138	  graph, and after 3 consecutive failures an alert is pushed to the workspace channel — once
139	  on the way down and once on recovery, never once per poll. The reason is always the
140	  **classified** one, never raw error text (the real failure carried a SAS token in its
141	  message).
142	- **Email OTP sign-in** — a third authenticator alongside dev-bypass and OIDC (ADR 0032):
143	  a one-time code emailed to an allow-listed address, `dq_sess_` cookie sessions, no
144	  Identity Provider required. Now the default for the local/eval stack (bundled Mailpit
145	  mail catcher), gated by one switch.
146	- **Workspace roles (Admin / Member / Viewer)** — stored, in-app-managed roles (ADR 0033)
147	  replace the old email-allowlist-only admin model; connection mutations are now
148	  Admin-only. `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` is a bootstrap/break-glass allowlist, not the
149	  primary mechanism.
150	- **`schema_drift` monitor kind** — flags added/removed/type-changed columns against a
151	  captured baseline, with a one-click re-baseline.
152	- **`comparison` checks** — cross-dataset reconciliation (row counts, column-level
153	  mismatch detection) between a suite's target and a second dataset (ADR 0015).
154	- **`anomaly` monitor kind** — a rolling z-score baseline with optional seasonality over a
155	  check's `metric_value` history; skips on cold start rather than false-alerting.
156	- **DQ-dimension classification** — every check carries a dimension (accuracy /
157	  completeness / consistency / integrity / timeliness / uniqueness / validity, ADR 0038),
158	  derived by default and overridable, feeding the new **asset DQ scorecard** — coverage by
159	  dimension, not just a pass rate.
160	- **Metric trend view** — a per-check history chart with threshold bands and an
161	  anomaly-baseline overlay.
162	- **Self-hosted secret store (OpenBao)** — a `SecretStore` backend speaking the KV v2 HTTP
163	  API (ADR 0039), alongside Azure Key Vault, for a non-Azure or self-hosted deployment.
164	- **Request rate limiting** — a fixed-window throttle across REST, webhooks, and `/mcp`
165	  (ADR 0035), with separate per-token / per-IP / per-webhook-provider classes.
166	- **S3-compatible endpoints** — the `s3` datasource and the `dbt` orchestration provider
167	  both accept an optional `endpoint_url` (+ addressing style), unlocking MinIO / Ceph / R2
168	  / Wasabi / Backblaze alongside AWS S3 (#1063).
169	- **Warehouse inventory sync** — an opt-in per-connection sweep (ADR 0040) that enumerates
170	  every table in a database, so a table with no suite/run/lineage edge shows up as
171	  visible-and-unmonitored instead of invisible.
172	- **PDF report export** — a zero-dependency, one-click PDF of a run's results.
173	
174	### Fixed
175	
176	- **Iceberg catalog credential exposure** — the SQL-catalog password had to be carried
177	  inline in the `catalog_uri` (the connection type had only one secret slot), which meant
178	  it was persisted in the connections table, copied into the asset identity, returned by
179	  the API, and rendered in the UI. Iceberg connections now take a **second secret**
180	  (`catalog_secret_name`), the config **rejects** a password in `catalog_uri`, and a
181	  migration scrubs existing rows. **Action required:** an existing Iceberg connection whose

## Checks & authoring

Every check is a Great Expectations expectation in v1 (`check.kind`), authored in the UI:

- **DQ dimension** — every check is classified by the quality aspect it measures
  (accuracy, completeness, consistency, integrity, timeliness, uniqueness, validity).
  It is filled in for you from the check type and stays editable; it powers the asset
  **scorecard** below. See [Datasources & checks](datasources-checks.md#dq-dimension-adr-0038).

- **GX expectations** — column- and table-shape rules (not-null, unique, in-set, row
  count, value ranges, …) from the GX catalog, with a form editor.
- **Custom SQL** — an escape hatch for cross-column/join rules: rows returned = failures.
  Read-only, single-statement (enforced). SQL datasources only.
- **Freshness monitor** — hours since the latest timestamp (is the data stale?). On a
  flat file you can leave the timestamp column blank, and it measures when the **file
  last landed** instead — which catches a producer that stopped sending files, something
  a timestamp inside the data cannot see.
- **Volume monitor** — row count within an expected range (did the load land whole?).
  Freshness + volume are the auto-monitor kinds and run on **every** datasource: the SQL
  datasources (Snowflake / Unity Catalog), Apache Iceberg (computed natively via a
  `pyiceberg` scan rather than SQL), and ADLS Gen2 / S3 flat files.
- **Schema-drift monitor** — flags a column added, dropped, or type-changed against a
  stored baseline (did the shape change under you?). Also runs on **every** datasource —
  introspection is per-store (SQL `information_schema`, a Parquet footer / CSV header
  sample for flat files, Iceberg table metadata), never a data scan.
- **Column profiler** — nulls, distinct count, min/max, and top values for a column, on
  any datasource — the baseline you set thresholds from.
- **Dry-run preview** — run one check against live data **without persisting**, on every
  datasource with a runner (Snowflake / UC / flat files / Iceberg).
- **Severity thresholds** — band a check into **warn / fail / critical** from the observed
  unexpected-% (ADR 0005/0016); leave blank for binary pass/fail.
- **Check version history** — every edit is versioned and viewable per check.

363:## Run it
===

### Schema-drift monitor (all datasources — ADR 0012, #592)

*Did the shape change under you?* Capture a **baseline** column-name/type snapshot,
then each run diffs the live snapshot against it and flags any add / drop /
type-change. Introspection is per-datasource, never a `CheckRunner`/GX pass or a
data scan: `information_schema` for Snowflake/Unity Catalog, the Parquet footer (or
a bounded CSV header sample) for ADLS Gen2/S3 flat files, and the loaded table's own
metadata for Iceberg. Re-baseline explicitly once you've reviewed a drift and want
it as the new normal — it is never re-baselined for you.

### DQ dimension (ADR 0038)

Every check carries a **DQ dimension** — the quality aspect it measures. This is a
third axis, separate from the check *kind* (how it works) and the expectation type
(the specific rule):

| Dimension | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Does the data match reality / a trusted source? |
| Completeness | Is all the expected data present? |
| Consistency | Do related datasets agree with each other? |
| Integrity | Do relationships between datasets hold? |
| Timeliness | Is the data recent enough? |
| Uniqueness | Are there unexpected duplicates? |
| Validity | Does the data conform to its rules and formats? |

**It is filled in for you.** The editor defaults it from the check type — a
not-null check is Completeness, a freshness monitor is Timeliness — and you can
change it at any time, including long after the check was created. Derivation is a
good guess about intent, not a fact: the same range check is *Validity* when it
bounds a percentage and *Accuracy* when it asserts a reconciled total.

Two dimensions are **never** guessed. **Accuracy** and **Integrity** can't be
inferred from the shape of a rule, and a **custom SQL** check is an arbitrary
predicate with no derivable answer at all — those start blank for you to set.

Leaving it blank is legitimate: the check is recorded as *unclassified* and shows
up as a **coverage gap** rather than being quietly filed under a dimension it
doesn't belong to. That matters because the point of dimensions is coverage —
"this table has no Timeliness checks at all" is the actionable finding, and it
would be a lie if unclassified checks were silently bucketed.

Checks created before this feature landed are unclassified until you next edit
them; they were deliberately not bulk-classified, so a derived guess is never
mistaken for someone's decision.

input.new_string:
Re-baseline explicitly once you've reviewed a drift and want
it as the new normal — it is never re-baselined for you.

### Anomaly monitor (Snowflake / Unity Catalog — ADR 0012, #593)

*Is this value abnormal for this dataset?* Where a volume monitor asks "is the row
count inside a range I chose?", the anomaly monitor learns the range: it keeps a
rolling mean/stddev of the target's own **row count** or **freshness age** and bands
each run's **z-score** through the usual warn / fail / critical thresholds. Optional
**seasonality** makes the baseline weekday-aware, so a quiet Sunday isn't an anomaly
just for being smaller than Monday.

Below its `min_points` of history the check reports **skip**, never a fabricated
pass — a baseline that hasn't seen enough runs has no opinion. The per-check
**trend view** overlays the learned baseline band on the metric history so you can
see what "normal" currently means. SQL datasources only: the anomaly executor takes
its own measurement over a live SQL connection, which the natively-computed Iceberg
and flat-file monitor paths don't expose.

### Comparison check (all datasources — ADR 0015)

*Does this dataset reconcile against that one?* A comparison check diffs the suite's
dataset (the **target under test**) against a **baseline** on any other datasource
connection — cross-type and cross-env both work (Snowflake DEV vs Snowflake QA, or
Snowflake vs the flat-file extract it was loaded from). Rows are joined on the key
columns you pick, producing **matched / mismatched / additional-per-side** buckets
with a mismatch-% metric that bands through the normal severity thresholds. Reads
are capped fail-fast (`COMPARISON_MAX_ROWS`), samples are redacted like every other
failing-row surface, and a CSV/XLSX report of the differences is downloadable
on demand (derived at read time, never stored). Either SQL side can use a read-only
query projection instead of a whole table.

## v1.1.0 — 2026-08-21

Portability, auto-monitors, compliance-grade controls, and polish on top of v1. (First
tagged 2026-08-15; the tag was moved to the true cycle close on 2026-08-21 after the
stretch week landed the RBAC, MCP-expansion, security-audit and compliance tracks below.)

- **Append-only audit trail (ADR 0041)** — every config mutation (35 routes: checks,
  connections, shares, roles, schedules, credential rotations, …) writes an `audit_events`
  row **inside the mutation's transaction**, with actor, before/after, and `request_id`;
  **data reads are audited too**: reading a run's results, downloading a comparison
  report, profiling a column or dry-running a check records who accessed which data and
  **whether regulated data was actually surfaced**. Workspace-admin read endpoint
  (`GET /api/v1/admin/audit-events`), own retention clock. Verified in production on both
  clouds.
- **Warehouse-tag PII classification** — DataQ reads the column classifications a
  customer already applied in their own warehouse (Snowflake `dataq_classification` +
  `PRIVACY_CATEGORY`, Unity Catalog `dataq_classification`) and feeds them into the
  redaction ladder as a floor a suite policy cannot lift — on REST, MCP and alert
  delivery. Plus an opt-in **fail-closed mode** (`require_classification`): nothing
  row-level surfaces unless a column is explicitly cleared. Live-verified on both
  warehouses.
- **Redaction follows the destination** — an author's own interactive preview keeps its
  values (and is audited); the same data headed to an LLM context, a file export or an
  alert is redacted. Scalar `observed_value`s (a MAX/MIN is a real cell) now mask under
  the same rules as lists, resolved against the check's **historical** config so editing
  a check can never retroactively relabel old results.
- **Residency & encryption posture** — a declared `DEPLOYMENT_REGION` surfaced at
  `GET /api/v1/admin/deployment`, an IaC postcondition that fails the plan if the compute
  environment leaves the declared region, and a per-resource encryption-at-rest table for
  both reference deployments in the security docs.
- **Compliance document set** — sub-processor disclosure, DPIA input sheet,
  breach-notification runbook, and counsel-gated DPA/BAA templates, published on the docs
  site.
- **Hardened containers** — the backend image now runs as a non-root user.

  provider-neutral OIDC (ADR 0026 amendment).

  beside per-suite grants; connection mutations are Admin-only. ⚠️ **Breaking:** Members

  posture documentation, and the compliance document set (sub-processors, DPIA input,
  breach runbook, DPA/BAA templates).

  refuses instead of SIGKILLing, with sampled-ness recorded per result.

  stores** (MinIO/R2/Wasabi/…); **dbt** as a third orchestration provider (ADR 0029);
  **OpenBao/Vault-API secret store** (ADR 0039); **warehouse inventory sync** (ADR 0040).

### Security

- Self-registration closed at the IdP **and** an app-side OIDC allowlist enforced per
  request; browser security headers (CSP, HSTS, …) on every response; CloudFront WAF +
  edge caching; nginx-enforced origin secret; backend image runs as **non-root**;
  Iceberg catalog credential moved out of `catalog_uri` (rotation required — see the
  docs changelog's Fixed entry); credential-redirect guard: a stored secret is never
  forwarded to a destination the caller just changed.

gh release create v1.1.0 --title "DataQ v1.1.0" --notes "The post-v1 cycle: **2026-07-04 → 2026-08-21** (six planned weeks + a stretch week; ~620 commits, 15 new ADRs — 0028–0041 plus the 0026 amendment). Tagged at the true cycle close — the stretch week alone added workspace RBAC, the MCP expansion, the security audit and the compliance track.

## Highlights

### The DQ platform leap
- **All monitor kinds real:** \`comparison\` (cross-dataset reconciliation, ADR 0015), \`schema_drift\`, and \`anomaly\` (rolling z-score baseline with seasonality) join freshness/volume — every check classified on the **DQ-dimension** axis (ADR 0038) and rolled into per-asset scorecards.
- **Assets, lineage & incidents (ADR 0034/0037):** the monitored table/file is a first-class entity — health rollup, OpenLineage-named identity, pulled lineage (dbt manifests, warehouse \`GET_LINEAGE\`, \`LineageProvider\`/Marquez), stateful deduped **incidents** with evidence cards, and the navigation inversion (assets lead the UI).
- **Scale-aware execution:** sampling + partition batching + an OOM guardrail that refuses instead of SIGKILLing, sampled-ness recorded per result.

### Reach
- **AWS as a second live reference deployment** (ECS Fargate + RDS + ElastiCache + Cognito + Secrets Manager behind CloudFront) beside Azure, on one generic provider-neutral image + OIDC contract; IaC on **OpenTofu**.
- **Apache Iceberg** as a fifth datasource (native \`pyiceberg\`, ADR 0030); **S3-compatible stores** (MinIO/R2/Wasabi/…); **dbt** as a third orchestration provider (ADR 0029); **OpenBao / Vault-API secret store** (ADR 0039); **warehouse inventory sync** (ADR 0040).

### Access & AI
- ⚠️ **Workspace roles — Admin / Member / Viewer (ADR 0033).** Connection mutations are now Admin-only. **Breaking:** promote connection-managing users to Admin before upgrading.
- **Email OTP sign-in** (ADR 0032, the local/eval default), **PATs** (\`dq_live_\`, ADR 0026), **rate limiting** (ADR 0035).
- **MCP server 8 → 46 tools** (23 read-only / 18 state-changing / 5 live-probe), with an honesty pass across all 46 — every tool states its blind spots as fields, not prose. No MCP tool is Admin-only; a credential never transits an LLM.

### Compliance & security
- **Append-only audit trail (ADR 0041):** every config mutation AND data read (results, comparison reports, profiles, dry-runs) recorded transactionally, admin-queryable, with whether regulated data was actually surfaced. Production-verified on both clouds.
- **Warehouse-tag PII classification** (Snowflake + Unity Catalog) feeding the redaction ladder as a floor a suite policy cannot lift, plus an opt-in fail-closed mode; redaction follows the **destination** (interactive preview vs LLM/file/alert).
- Security-surface audit of both deployments: self-registration closed (IdP + app-side allowlist), full browser security headers with enforcing CSP, CloudFront WAF + edge caching, non-root backend image, residency declaration + IaC region postcondition, compliance document set (sub-processors, DPIA input, breach runbook, DPA/BAA templates).
